parallel.requirements: The run recognized a clean-room reverse-engineering obligation: reproduce the bundled `genact` executable behavior from docs and CLI observation without source lookup, binary wrapping, or disassembly.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent owned final implementation and delivery while three children were assigned read-only module-observation work; no child was made owner of a production component.
parallel.implementation: After probing the CLI and receiving child observations, the parent implemented a dependency-free Rust executable with manual parser behavior, static surfaces, scene generators, and an offline compile script.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent integrated observations itself, wrote `Cargo.toml`, `compile.sh`, and `src/main.rs`, built a release binary, copied it to `./executable`, and left build outputs in the artifact.
parallel.verification: The parent compared help, version, invalid module and speed errors, TTY panic cases, manpage/completion snippets, and representative scene samples, then official evaluation still failed.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator recorded 114 failing tests, so hidden behavioral coverage remained incomplete even though the parent delivered a compiling executable.

serial.requirements: The run recognized the same clean-room obligation and avoided source lookup or wrapping, relying on docs plus observed CLI and runtime transcripts.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single parent owned discovery, implementation, integration, verification, and delivery, with no child-agent or handoff lifecycle.
serial.implementation: The parent first drafted a Rust implementation with external crates, hit offline dependency failure, then pivoted to a standalone Go implementation with embedded static assets and scene generators.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The parent wrote `main.go`, `compile.sh`, assets for manpage and completions, removed the abandoned Rust draft, built `./executable`, and left a coherent Go submission.
serial.verification: The serial run checked help, version, module listing, manpage, completions, invalid argument cases, executable permissions, and representative `memdump` and `weblog` runtime output.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator recorded 132 failing tests, so the Go implementation also missed substantial hidden behavior despite successful local spot checks.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the reverse-engineering constraints and observed `genact 1.5.1` CLI behavior before implementing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same clean-room task, docs, binary, module list, generated artifacts, and parser constraints.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement recognition was materially similar; parallel had broader concurrent observation but no different official pass outcome.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent delegated module observations to three children while retaining implementation, integration, build, and final delivery ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no subagents and kept the entire discovery-to-delivery pipeline in one parent thread.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel split reconnaissance only; serial remained centralized. Neither run lacked an implementation or assembly owner.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children returned module reports; the parent noticed one conflicting repeated-`--modules` observation and resolved it with direct probes before implementation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept observations in one thread, including the same repeated module and invalid argument checks, so no inter-agent context transfer was needed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced a handoff boundary but adjudicated the conflict, while serial avoided handoff risk by centralizing the evidence.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote a Rust implementation, first with dependencies and then as a dependency-free std-only rewrite after offline crate access failed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote a Rust draft, found crates unavailable, pivoted to a standalone Go implementation, embedded static assets, and removed the Rust draft.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The implementation language and packaging differed; both were ordinary engineering choices rather than parallel coordination failures.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel waited for child agents, received final reports from mods_c, mods_a, and mods_b, and then continued implementation with their findings.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle because multi-agent features were disabled and all observations stayed in the parent.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel added join overhead but no lost child result or trapped verifier result; serial had no comparable join boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children did not write implementation files; the parent alone patched source and compile script, then built and copied the release executable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also wrote implementation files from one parent, later cleaned out the abandoned Rust draft so only the Go path remained.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There was no observed parallel write collision or shared-state contamination; serial had simpler provenance but lower official score.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verified local builds and representative CLI, parser, TTY panic, manpage, completion, and scene behaviors, then official evaluation still failed 114 tests.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verified local builds, static surfaces, invalid arguments, executable permission, and representative memdump and weblog runs, then official evaluation still failed 132 tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both relied on representative spot checks rather than exhaustive behavioral parity; parallel scored better but neither reached full acceptance.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel finished within the cell budget, used three children for early exploration, completed release build checks, and closed with a final response.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial finished within the cell budget after longer single-thread exploration and a Rust-to-Go pivot, then closed with a final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Neither attempt timed out. Parallel fan-out increased observation breadth and official score, but no budget exhaustion or late finalization episode materialized.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both official completed evaluations failed. The parallel run produced a Rust implementation after using three child agents to broaden module observation and scored 123/237; the serial run produced a Go implementation after a Rust dependency pivot and scored 105/237. The score gap plausibly reflects broader parallel observation and different ordinary implementation coverage, but there is no discordant outcome and no directly evidenced adverse parallel coordination episode explaining a pass/fail split.
parallel_contributors: Parallel used child agents for module-family probing and parent-side implementation, giving broader early observation coverage.
The parent resolved a conflicting repeated-module observation with direct probes before coding.
serial_contributors: Serial kept all observations in one parent thread and eventually pivoted to a standalone Go implementation.
Serial cleaned out the abandoned Rust draft and verified a coherent final build path.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel delivered a Rust implementation with generated cargo artifacts while serial delivered a Go implementation with embedded completion and manpage assets.
Both implementations were based on representative sampling rather than exhaustive parity, leaving many hidden evaluator failures.
evaluator_effects: The official summaries expose only pass/failure counts, not the individual hidden behavioral mismatches.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; supported comparison only, not an exclusive root cause
